$comment: GitGit required status-check contexts — the JOB NAMES that the branch protection is expected to require. GitHub reports a check under a job's `name:`, so these strings are the context strings: changing one of them here without changing the protection leaves the protection requiring a check that is never reported, which is the same deadlock as a path-filtered workflow, one string away. The names below are the EXISTING job names, character for character, which is why adding them to the branch protection cannot silently miss. The deep-gate refactor (docs/plan/deep-gate-enforcement.md) moved the path filter from the workflow level into the jobs, so these jobs now report on EVERY pull request — a job skipped by its own `if:` condition is reported as 'Success', which satisfies a required check, whereas a workflow that never starts reports nothing and leaves the check Pending forever. NOT ENFORCED YET: as of this commit the GitHub branch protection still requires only `repo gate (always runs)`. This file is the declared list, not the enforcement.

notes.enforcementNote: [FACT] The branch protection on GitHub is NOT changed by this commit. It still requires only `repo gate (always runs)`. Turning the contexts below into required checks is a separate, deliberate step, and it has to be verified empirically on GitHub afterwards with a real pull request (a docs-only one must show all five contexts green, and one that touches src/** must show the Rust gates actually running).
notes.laneScope: [FACT] These five contexts are the ones lane L1-a owns: the three rust-backend.yml jobs, the one gm-console.yml job, and the one frontend-audit.yml job. gm-desktop.yml and gm-desktop-bundle.yml still carry workflow-level path filters and are lane L1-b; their job names are deliberately NOT listed here, because listing a context whose workflow is still path-filtered would put the branch protection back into the Pending-forever deadlock.
notes.verification: [UNVERIFIED-FACT] GitHub's path-matching component is not open source, so the local equivalence between scripts/ci/changed-areas.ps1 and GitHub's own `paths:` semantics is an inference, not a fact. The real verification is the empirical pull-request check described above.
